classification.classification_note: The reproduced memory error is a stack-buffer-overflow WRITE into local `char str[1024]` in `diST_box_read()`.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42507999 (gpac): Stack-buffer-overflow WRITE 1 found by fuzz target fuzz_parse [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42507999
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source / staged poc / staged src/utils/bitstream.c
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced the issue against the staged vulnerable GPAC source snapshot at `ee87237997f520f3c86512b39923343ff0877188`. The exact staged 1032-byte witness is a single root `diST` box: bytes 0..3 encode total size `0x00000020` (32), bytes 4..7 encode type `diST`, bytes 8..13 are `20 ff ff ff ff ff`, and bytes 14..1031 are ASCII space `0x20`. In `gf_isom_box_parse_ex()`, GPAC reads `size == 32`, records `hdr_size = 4` after the size word, reads the `diST` type, increments `hdr_size` to 8, and derives `newBox->size = 24` as the payload length passed into `diST_box_read()`. Vulnerable `diST_box_read()` then stages the string in fixed stack buffer `char str[1024]` and loops until `gf_bs_read_u8()` returns zero, with no bound on either `i < sizeof(str)` or the remaining payload length `s->size`. On the exact witness, all 1024 bytes after the 8-byte header are nonzero, so the loop fills `str[0..1023]`, never takes the `if (!str[i]) break` exit, and continues far past the declared 24-byte payload because `ISOM_DECREASE_SIZE(p, i)` runs only after the loop. The next read reaches EOF, `gf_bs_read_u8()` logs `[BS] Attempt to overread bitstream` and returns 0, and `diST_box_read()` writes that zero to `str[1024]`, producing the saved `AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 1` at `src/isomedia/box_code_3gpp.c:1116`. The staged patch fixes the bug by allocating `s->size + 1` bytes, reading exactly `s->size` bytes with `gf_bs_read_data`, and appending the terminator in bounds.

source.description: First project parser statement on the vulnerable path. `gf_isom_box_parse_ex()` materializes the attacker-controlled root-box size and starts the header-size bookkeeping later used to derive the payload length passed to `diST_box_read()`.
source.value_from: The exact staged `poc` is the 1032-byte file at `gt_results/arvo_42507999/poc` with SHA-256 `50bf7dbd0be8d974396fb410be4e505ea7cf93be3f96ee6a163ea3f24fc19b52`. Its first four bytes are `00 00 00 20`, so this statement pair materializes `size == 32` from attacker-controlled input and records that 4 header bytes have already been consumed.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The `diST` string reader is controlled only by a sentinel-NUL loop and never bounds `i` against the fixed `str[1024]` extent or checks the remaining payload length `s->size` before each byte read.
root_cause.note: The patch removes this loop and instead allocates `s->size + 1` bytes, reads exactly `s->size` bytes with `gf_bs_read_data`, and appends an in-bounds terminator at `p->content_script_types[s->size] = 0`.

sink.description: ASan sink. After 1024 non-NUL bytes have advanced `i` to 1024, this assignment writes one byte to `str[1024]`, one byte past the 1024-byte stack buffer.
sink.note: The saved trace reports `WRITE of size 1` at `src/isomedia/box_code_3gpp.c:1116:10` and identifies `str` in `diST_box_read` as stack object `[32, 1056)`. The preceding runtime log `[BS] Attempt to overread bitstream` matches staged `src/utils/bitstream.c`, where `BS_ReadByte()` returns 0 at EOF and explains the one-byte terminating write.

tainted_value_origin.description: This statement materializes each attacker-controlled file byte into the stack buffer. On the exact witness the first 1024 executions copy 1024 consecutive nonzero bytes into `str[0..1023]`.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: After the 8-byte header, the staged witness contains 1024 nonzero bytes and no NUL terminator: bytes 8..13 are `20 ff ff ff ff ff` and bytes 14..1031 are `0x20`. Those 1024 bytes drive the repeated writes before the final EOF read returns 0.

parser_admitted.description: After the root box header is accepted and `newBox->size` is derived, GPAC dispatches the parsed `diST` box into its type-specific reader `diST_box_read()`.

evidence_limitations: `trace_feedback.json` required explicitly closing the `hdr_size` derivation feeding `newBox->size`; this rebuild records `hdr_size = 4` and `hdr_size += 4` as separate source-level transitions. `run_flags.json` keeps `runtime_disambiguation` disabled and the reviewer did not request it, so Stage 02 remained source-grounded and added no instrumentation.

Stage 01 saved only the final ASan report and the single `[BS] Attempt to overread bitstream` log line, not per-iteration loop telemetry. The 1024-iteration fill of `str[0..1023]` is therefore reconstructed from the exact 1032-byte witness layout plus the staged loop and EOF semantics in the vulnerable source.

fine_trace.note: Source. The first four attacker-controlled bytes `00 00 00 20` are read as `size == 32`, and the parser records that the size word already accounts for 4 bytes of box header.
The next four input bytes are `64 69 53 54` (`diST`), so this root box is identified as `GF_ISOM_BOX_TYPE_DIST` and later dispatched to `diST_box_read()`.
Charging the type word increases `hdr_size` from 4 to 8 on this witness, making the full root-box header length explicit before payload-size arithmetic.
Using `size == 32` from step 1 and `hdr_size == 8` from step 3, the parser stores `newBox->size == 24`, the remaining payload length later seen as `s->size` in `diST_box_read()`.
Destination extent. Once the `diST` reader runs, it stages the incoming string in fixed stack buffer `str[1024]` instead of allocating from the 24-byte payload length carried in `s->size`.
The write index starts at 0 for the first byte copied into `str`.

Root cause. Loop continuation is controlled only by the later `if (!str[i]) break`; there is no `i < sizeof(str)` bound and no per-byte check of `s->size` before reading. The only box-size guard, `ISOM_DECREASE_SIZE(p, i)`, appears after the loop, so it cannot stop the out-of-bounds iteration.

All 1024 bytes at file offsets 8..1031 are nonzero (`20 ff ff ff ff ff` followed by 1018 spaces). The first 24 iterations consume the declared payload, but because step 7 never consults `s->size`, the loop continues through the extra file bytes. Across these 1024 executions the break never fires, `str[0..1023]` become attacker-controlled nonzero bytes, and `i` advances to 1024.

Sink. With `i == 1024` from step 8, the next `gf_bs_read_u8()` requests byte 1032, which is past the 1032-byte witness. Staged `BS_ReadByte()` logs `[BS] Attempt to overread bitstream` and returns 0 at EOF, and this assignment writes that 0 to `str[1024]`, one byte past the stack buffer. The saved ASan report records `WRITE of size 1` at this exact line and identifies `str` as stack object `[32, 1056)` in `diST_box_read`.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: Yes at the source level. The patch replaces the fixed stack buffer and unbounded byte-at-a-time loop with `gf_malloc(s->size + 1)`, `gf_bs_read_data(..., s->size)`, and an in-bounds terminator write.

poc.trigger: Running the staged witness under the Stage 01 vulnerable ARVO workspace reproduces `AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 1` in `diST_box_read`, matching `reproduction_report.json` and `sanitizer_trace.txt`.

format.name: Single root ISO BMFF `diST` box
format.contract: The verified trigger is the exact 1032-byte file staged at `gt_results/arvo_42507999/poc` (SHA-256 `50bf7dbd0be8d974396fb410be4e505ea7cf93be3f96ee6a163ea3f24fc19b52`). Bytes 0..3 encode size `0x00000020` (32), bytes 4..7 are ASCII `diST`, bytes 8..13 are `20 ff ff ff ff ff`, and bytes 14..1031 are `0x20`. This means the vulnerable parser sees payload length 24, but the file still provides 1024 consecutive non-NUL bytes after the 8-byte header. On the saved vulnerable path `diST_box_read()` copies the first 1024 of those bytes into `char str[1024]` without ever seeing a terminator or consulting `s->size`; the next `gf_bs_read_u8()` call reaches EOF, returns 0, and that zero is written to `str[1024]`, reproducing the saved ASan stack-buffer-overflow WRITE. The staged artifacts do not justify a broader trigger than this exact witness layout and observed `diST` path.
